claim_risk_summary: Fooks et al. studied British American Tobacco CSR, not a validated cross-sector civic-sponsorship maturity model.
The statement that civic institutions become participants in lobbying strategies regardless of intent is an overgeneralized inference.
Federal tax, gift-acceptance, procurement, ethics and First Amendment rules differ from private nonprofit governance and are omitted.
The 20% revenue ceiling, quarterly independent monitoring and maturity tiers are authored proposals, not universal legal or evidence-based standards.
Commercial outcome claims and both anonymous PIONEERING examples are unsupported.

P0: CSP blocks Chart.js; assessment cannot advance after first response.
P1: Promised PDF is never invoked and its dependency is blocked.
Instrument does not measure six stated dimensions: all item pairs are duplicates and all answer ladders are generic.
Civic/government/legal framing lacks jurisdiction, public-body, procurement, gift-acceptance and constitutional boundaries.
Hidden screens remain exposed to assistive technology and the modal is not accessible.
Lead forms can claim or imply success without a successful API response.

verification_boundaries: No consequential result, contact, waitlist, booking or purchase submission was made.

No installed browser binary was available; browser automation could not be completed. Runtime failure is deterministic from matching deployed source, CSP and dependency origins, but live focus/reflow/device observations remain required.
API persistence, report email, retention, deletion, rate limiting and abuse controls remain unverified.
Toolkit existence, six-source evidence base, templates, terms and fulfillment remain unverified.
No psychometric, content-validity, reliability or outcome validation was supplied.
